parameters.content:
## 🚀 SETUP GUIDE - read this first

**What this workflow does:** user sends a topic on Telegram → AI script → voiceover + video render → finished Short comes back on Telegram, with a status message after every step.

### 0. Prerequisites
- The **worker** (Node `server.js`), **renderer** (Remotion), **Postgres** and **n8n** run in the *same Docker network*, so n8n can reach `http://worker:5000`.
- Worker `.env` has `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `POSTGRES_*` etc. (never commit that file).

### 1. Create the Telegram bot
Open **@BotFather** → `/newbot` → copy the **bot token**.

### 2. Add the credential in n8n
**Credentials → Add credential → Telegram API** → paste the token → Save.
Then open **every Telegram node** (the trigger + all `Notify:` / `Error:` nodes + `Send a video`) and pick that credential. (Credentials are NOT stored in this file.)

### 3. Check the worker URL
All HTTP nodes call `http://worker:5000`. If your compose service name or port differs, change it in: *Generate Video Script, Create Video Job, Process Video Job, Download Generated Video, Get Job Error Details*.

### 4. Telegram needs a public HTTPS webhook
Set n8n env `WEBHOOK_URL=https://your-domain` (use ngrok / Cloudflare Tunnel for local testing), restart n8n, then **Activate** the workflow.

### 5. Test
Send your bot a message in the format shown in the note below.

### 🔒 Before pushing to GitHub
- Credentials, webhook ids and instance id were removed from this file.
- Never commit the bot token, `.env` or API keys.
- After importing, re-select the Telegram credential on each Telegram node.

### 📩 Message format
```
Topic: JavaScript Array Methods
Audience: Beginners
Language: Hinglish
Duration: 30 seconds
```
Duration: 1-180 seconds (worker limit).

### 🔔 Progress messages (green path)
One Telegram message after each step: request received → script ready → job created → video rendered → video sent. Edit the text of any `Notify:` node freely. They all use the chat id of the person who messaged the bot.

### ⏳ Slow step
`Process Video Job` does voiceover + render in one call, so it can take several minutes (timeout 15 min). If the job is already running, the worker answers 409 and you get a render error message.

### ❌ Error messages (red path)
Every HTTP node has *On Error → Continue (using error output)*. Its red output goes to an `Error:` node that tells the user **which step failed and why**.
`Get Job Error Details` reads the exact failure reason saved by the worker (`error_message`), so keep the worker on the latest `server.js`.
